[h1]DESYNC: Un Viaje Neon de Disparos y Glitchs[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
Si eras de los que se excitaban con los juegos de disparos arcade de los 80 pero a la vez eras el fanboy número uno de Tron, entonces, ¡bienvenido a DESYNC! Este juego es la mezcla perfecta de disparos frenéticos, neon por doquier, y una sensación constante de \¿pero qué demonios está pasando aquí?\. Es como entrar en la discoteca más rara del mundo, pero en vez de bailar, te dedicas a disparar a criaturas digitales que parecen haber salido de una pesadilla de Matrix. 

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
DESYNC ataca con un estilo visual que es un deleite en ácido cibernético. Los colores y los efectos visuales son tan intensos que podrías considerar ponerte unas gafas de sol mientras juegas. La música electrónica te mete completamente en el ambiente y te hace sentir como si realmente estuvieras en un rave de videojuegos de los años 80. ¿Y la jugabilidad? Rápida, furiosa y casi a punto de romperte los dedos de puro frenesí.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
Claro, no todo es una fiesta rave colorida. El juego puede ser despiadadamente difícil, lo que a veces hace que quieras lanzar tu control contra la pared (o la pantalla, no te culpo). Además, la trama es más confusa que explicarle Reddit a tus abuelos. Si pudieran pulir estos aspectos, DESYNC podría pasar de ser un buen juego de disparos a un clásico de culto.

This is a really great game and it's a shame to hear about it being delisted. Let me attempt to do it justice. This is an Arena shooter with the movement mechanics of Doom Eternal. You shoot and dash around quickly to a thumping EDM soundtrack while pulling off scored kills. There are dozens and dozens of finishers which will net you a larger score and more dropped supplies so the name of the game is to kill quickly and with style.

It took a few hours for things to fall into place but once it does this quickly becomes a pulse-pounding joy. Make no mistake about it this is a modern 'boomer shooter' before the term even existed. Many of the design elements in this game are only now just being explored by other throwback FPS games. It deserves a bigger place in the pantheon of our genre. 

If you want to know what holds this game back here we go. Be prepared for zero explanation of the upgrade system. You will have to remember weird names and shapes of the various weapons, items, and power ups. Newly collected weapons often leave you guessing what their sub functions are. Power ups and abilities aren't really explained clearly so you'll have to experiment (re: waste) them frequently until you learn what they actually do. Also, there is a somewhat confusing fatality system that you use to score big and unlock upgrades. Even after 15 hours it is only slightly starting to make sense to me and i can barely remember a half a dozen of the massive list of options. 

Regardless this game is excellent and should be preserved in your collection. I encourage you to pick this up even if now isn't the right time to play it. When you come back around to it i bet you will be plesantly surprised.

Before the "Devil May Quake" of ULTRAKILL, and before the ammo-starved weapon-juggling Doom Eternal, there was DESYNC. Borrowing heavily from the skillshots of Bulletstorm while upping the complexity of the game mechanics and the difficulty of the combat encounters, DESYNC sought to translate the stylish but ballbusting aggression of character action games like Ninja Gaiden and Devil May Cry into an arcadey FPS. And it is tough. But like its inspirations, it expects the player to be humble: yes, you will die, and when you don't die, you'll get crappy ranks. But if you stick with it and learn from your mistakes, the game will give you new weapons, abilities, and upgrades to expand the ways you can engage with the combat. 

Eventually you'll go from feeling boxed in and abused to seeing the wide range of possibilities you have to interpret a fight, ultimately realizing the true creativity that it's been slowly trying to teach you all along. And then, after beating the final boss and seeing the credits, the real game begins: replaying the levels with a full arsenal, splattering baddies with style and grace, entirely on your own terms.

You may have specific ideas of what an FPS should be. Maybe you think it should be like the old school days, bunnyhopping and straferunning around labyrinths and popping monsters with a well placed shotgun blast from your nearly bottomless stores of ammo. Maybe you think it should be running down corridors, tossing grenades around corners and headshotting soldiers that pop out of cover.

DESYNC does not care what you think. DESYNC knows what it wants to be, and demands you play it on its terms, or it will kill you over and over until you learn or give up. This may be insulting to you. You may believe that its way is not fun, that it doesn't have the right to decide to be something different. DESYNC is not interested in your arguments. It knows that it's different, and it knows that the ways that it's different allows for a uniquely expressive and exciting approach to FPS gameplay. It knows it's fun, and it doesn't care if you don't believe it.

If you like a game that is against you in every aspect and punishes even the slightest of mistakes due to its own incompetence, this game is for you. 
Despite the claim to a fast-paced shooter, you'll most likely find yourself running away from tracking projectiles and enemy types that also somehow track you with melee damage. You are extremely weak and squishy in this game and even the grunts do quite a lot of damage, not to mention that health is based on random pickups that can fall into stage hazards that litter every single arena. 

Speaking of arenas and stage hazards, every combat encounter is filled with useless traps that either come in handy for 1/30 enemies if you have a certain gun type (only four can be equipped and one of those slots is specific to the starting pistol) or just block certain parts of the arena off because as stated previously you are squishy and you will die if you get anywhere near random traps. Have you ever been killed by a jump pad? Well apparently what is usually a fun air combat mechanic is actually just another method of preventing you from having fun with the decent gunplay. The good, open stages shown in the steam videos are very few in the actual game.

Movement is another downside--you are completely grounded in this game. Jumps are extremely short, there is no real means of becoming airborne, and the only extra movement option of "dodging" doesn't really work most of the time because enemies block your path and projectiles track your dodge even if you use the input immediately after a far away attack. 

Overall the game can be really inconsistent and slow-paced. The guns are cool and the combat is actually pretty fun, but stages and movement are awful. Challenge mode is borderline impossible for the same reasons with the added bonus of getting one-shot and killing enemies that explode very randomly. Unfortunately DESYNC is just not a fun game, and definitely not worth the full price.

Desync is an arcadey fast-paced arena-shooter. It has a unique art style and plays like very few other shooters out there. While I greatly enjoyed my time with it, it has a ton of little annoyances that may make the game a drag for some. In addition, it's rather short, with a roughly ~3 hour runtime! I'd suggest it on sale, but you should know what you're in for.

The combat is fast-paced and frantic. If you've played Bulletstorm, certain aspects of the combat might feel familiar. Desync has a strong focus on combos and juggling enemies. Unique enemy kills reward you with points and pickups in addition to ocassional powerups. Most of the weapons are very strong (though the final weapon is worse than the pistol), with the shotgun and railgun being a ton of fun to use. The railgun is loud and hits like a truck, and the shotgun has a tendency to send enemies cartwheeling through the air into hazards. Bosses are also very fun and mostly provide a reasonable challenge, though the 2nd boss requires some luck.

However, the combat is certainly not without flaws. The combat is reliant on dashing, which cannot be done in midair. This is a gigantic problem as it means that jumping is often punished by homing projectiles (almost all projectiles in the game are homing, by the way). Having to constantly repair your weapons is a major nuisance, and it's generally hard to tell when to do it without taking your focus away from the action. A durability indicator on the crosshair would have made this game outright better.

You have a fair bit of leeway in customizing your loadout. You can choose 3 weapons from the game's roster at a time. You can upgrade numerous stats of each weapon at the cost of other stats. You have a handful of powerups you can select, and you can make certain kills/combos grant special buffs for a short period of time. There's a handful of sidearm powerups you can select, though the only one I found worthwhile was the ice crossbow. The major problem with all of this customization is that it's rather complex and the game does a poor job explaining most of it. The desynchronization and weapon customization systems especially need to give the player more information. Desynchronizations are supposed to be a fundamental mechanic, but I was only able to make use of them a couple times throughout the whole game.

Level design tends to be rather mediocre - arenas are rather generic and only a handful of them have anything that set them apart. They're all fully functional but they followed a very predictable design philosophy. Almost every arena was symmetrical with two levels of verticality and spike traps dotted around pivotal points. A lot of environmental hazards feel like they are placed to annoy the player rather than help them perform combos. This was especially bad in the last episode, where the devs put small puddles of instant-death acid in obnoxious spots.

Finally, enemy design is a little mixed too. Most enemies were fine, but the abundance of homing projectiles is obnoxious in some arenas. The worst enemy in the game is the teleporting melee enemy that is capable of two-shotting you without warning. I absolutely hate these things, and they always have to take maximum priority whenever they spawn in. The obligatory shield enemy is rather obnoxious, but thankfully, the railgun mostly mitigates him. There's also the scorpion-esque enemy, who isn't too hard but feels far too damage spongey.

Would I recommend Desync? Yes, but you probably shouldn't get it unless it's on sale. While it's certainly replayable (I know I went back and replayed some levels), it's simply rather short. There are only 9 regular levels and 3 boss levels with a handful of optional gimmicky levels on the side. Ultimately, I got it for $3 and was highly satisfied.

スタイリッシュアクションFPS。
　良くも悪くも、2DアクションゲームをそのままFPSにしたらこうなるだろうなという感じ。
　ハイスピードでショットガンやらロケランやらのド派手な武器で敵を蹴散らしてステージを進んでいくため、サクサク進んでいけるときは爽快感がある。

　ただ、視界外でも敵は発生する上に、落ちると即死の穴や罠が随所に設置されているため、正面の敵の対処をしている最中に横で沸いた敵に攻撃されて死ぬなんてことがザラというかそれが大半の死因なところが結構ストレス。
　UIで敵が発生する位置を表示してくれてはいるが、見やすいわけではないため私では全く認識できなかった。そのため、基本的にはリトライを繰り返して敵がどこで沸くかを把握しておく死に覚えゲーだと考えておいたほうが良い。

　操作感は良いし、死んでもリトライがとても早いためその部分のストレスはほとんどない。敵を爆風で罠に吹き飛ばして罠でキルを取ったり、複数の敵を同時に倒したりするとコンボ判定が入りスコアがどんどん加算されていく。複数の敵を同時に罠に叩き込めば大量のスコアログが縦に並ぶ。楽しい。

　スピード感あるアクションとコンボを重ねる爽快感がとても楽しいゲームだと思う。ステージクリア後もスピードクリアやコンボでハイスコアを突き詰めていく楽しみ方もできるよ。

This is one of the freshest First Person shooters that I have come across. You are an entity:: robot: AI, sort that is within a program, and you have multiple sectors within , where you explore your inner capabilities to eliminate threats.
You get continuous upgrades as you play, to your weapons, or attacks, or you could lose certain upgrades for the challenge of a new level. It varies A LOT, and that's really fresh.
It looks digital, in all ways, and you behave as fluidly as the system you are within. It's very straight-forward. You complete a set of missions within the certain realm of your choosing, and whatever it unlocks, you'll see it back at your mainframe to be able to pick it up , if you want, or continue about the same way.

There are things to find within the levels you go into, although I'm so new into this, I'll have to tell you what the shards unlock as you go.

The sexy part of this game is keeping scores per level -  and your methods of killing them ie. as they spawn, as you charge, headshots, from behind, etc. count towards your total score.
The accuracy is also tracked.
It all feels like a digital simulation in the end of a level, but that's how rigorous the AI assesses your method of eliminating threats. It's like a digital Transformers-TotalOverdose

关卡比较少，花了9元特价买的，感觉9元才对得起这个游戏的内容，高了就对不起了。

细细想来，我因为听不见脚步声被围，暴毙好几回，你的血量对于敌人来说不够锤两下的，特别是到中后期，如果没有高超的走位技术，打盾熊只能浪费极其有限弹药，对于绝大部分FPS玩家是极度劝退的。
